intro: On Akdamar Island, out in Lake Van in Van province, stands a monument whose story runs from the 10th century AD to today: the Church of the Holy Cross, famous for its carved reliefs.
history: The church was built in 915–921 for King Gagik I by the architect-monk Manuel, and it served as the royal church of the Kingdom of Vaspurakan. Look at its exterior walls: the biblical reliefs carved there are unique in the world.
structure-1: You are now standing before the Church of the Holy Cross, the relief-carved church on Akdamar Island, built for King Gagik I in 915–921. Let your eyes travel slowly across its walls and read the stories carved in stone.
structure-5: Here is the cemetery, the ancient necropolis that lies outside the settlement. Walk quietly here, with respect for those laid to rest.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Palace Ruins, the Jetty and the Harbour.
facts: Did you know? On 19 September 2010 a service was held in the church for the first time in some 95 years, and one has been held every year since. The exterior of the Church of the Holy Cross, built for King Gagik I between 915 and 921, is covered wall to wall in relief: Jonah, David and Goliath, vine scrolls and animals. And in 2007 the church was restored and opened as a museum.
outro: This brings our visit to Akdamar Island to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Take one last look at the carved walls before you leave the island. Enjoy your visit.
